correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts every squarefree shape. If a squarefree composite has at least two odd prime factors, then \(4\mid\sigma(n)+\varphi(n)\) and the sum exceeds \(8\); since \(\tau(N)=4\) means \(N=p^3\) or \(N=pq\), the only such \(N\) divisible by \(4\) is \(8\), a contradiction. The sole remaining composite shape is \(2q\), where \(2(2q+1)\) reduces the divisor count exactly to primality of \(2q+1\).
